messages:
mia (eng-arch): Follow-up on negotiator handshake: we want a tiny stable contract so runtime doesn't need policy internals. Ideas?

sam (runtime): Strong yes. Right now policy returns huge graphs. Runtime only uses ~3 fields.

rafa (infra): +observability concern. If negotiator hides reasoning, SREs get blind spots. We need explain tokens and a run_id.

nina (product): Also need determinism for tiered SLAs. Customers on latency-tier "A" must never be dropped to a lower tier unless explicit fallback.

mia (eng-arch): Proposed minimal payload shape (v1): candidates: [route], compat: {route: enum}, scores: {route: {latency_ms, cost_token, region_affinity}}, fallbacks: [[r1,r2]]. Keep it flat JSON.

sam (runtime): Runtime wants optional single-number weight for quick heuristics: weight = alpha*latency + beta*cost + tenant_penalty. Make it optional.

rafa (infra): Telemetry list: negotiator_version, run_id, explain_token, policy_rev, candidate_list, chosen_candidate, runtime_decision, preempted:true|false, fallback_triggered. Retention 90 days for traces.

nina (product): UX: Console needs to simulate negotiator output for a tenant so product can preview routing before rollout. Standardized payload helps a lot.

mia (eng-arch): Enforcement semantics: mark candidates with enforced=true when tenant-level constraints apply. Runtime must prefer enforced candidates; only follow documented fallbacks after explicit consent.

sam (runtime): Implementation trade-offs: Option 1 runtime strictly follows ordered candidates -> simple but brittle. Option 2 runtime uses scores + local capacity heuristics -> resilient but more complex. I prefer Option 2 behind a feature flag.

rafa (infra): If go with Option 2, expose score->decision deltas in telemetry so we can alert when runtime deviates from negotiator expectations.

mia (eng-arch): Migration plan: v1 emit candidates+compat+scores. Runtime ignores scores (pass-through). v1.1 opt-in soft scoring. v2 add enforced flags + detailed compatibility breakdown (region/model/legal). Canary 3->10->50% tenants.

nina (product): We should provide an admin override in Console to force-enforce a candidate for emergencies. Only admins with 2FA.

sam (runtime): I'll add explain_token per candidate and a tiny shim in router to read v1 payload. Shim will log run_id and explain_token for each decision.

deploy-bot: deployment: negotiator-shim v1 rolled to staging cluster eu-central-1 (4 pods) - ticket INF-1499

rafa (infra): Make sure compat enum semantics are documented: soft-incompatible means runtime can still try if forced; incompatible means never. Later we split by reason: region/model/tenancy.

mia (eng-arch): Good point. For v1 keep single enum but doc the semantics. v2 expands compatibility map.

sam (runtime): PR incoming with JSON schema examples and a tiny python snippet showing weight combine() usage. Will add feature-flag toggles.

nina (product): I'll link Console simulation story to the PR and add a short acceptance criteria: "Console shows top 3 candidates and highlights enforced ones."

mia (eng-arch): Action items: sam - PR + shim prototype; rafa - telemetry fields + retention/alerts; nina - Console simulation story; I'll update RFC follow-up with versioning and migration checklist.

sam (runtime): PR by EOD.

rafa (infra): I'll post the telemetry YAML and alert rules in the PR comments.

nina (product): Scheduling the Console spike for next sprint.

mia (eng-arch): Thanks team. If anyone wants to argue about weight coefficients or enforced semantics, please add to the PR thread. :rocket:
